description:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

 


Role Overview

We're seeking a Senior AI Enablement Engineer to be the dedicated technical partner for Harvey's go-to-market organization — Sales, Customer Success, SDR, Legal Engineering, Partnerships, and Revenue Operations. GTM has been Harvey's most enthusiastic adopter of AI: teams have built dozens of skills, plugins, and agents on their own. That energy is an asset, but it has outrun the structure around it. Your job is to turn that energy into a focused set of workflows that GTM teams trust and use every day.

This is a hands-on technical IC role inside BizTech (Business Technology), partnering closely with GTM leaders, GTM Systems, and RevOps. You'll spend your time sitting with sellers, SDRs, and CSMs to understand how they actually work; consolidating and hardening the workflows worth keeping and retiring the ones that aren't; building the connector and MCP integrations those workflows depend on; and giving GTM a fast, clear answer when they want to try something new. The ideal candidate is a senior IC engineer who understands how a revenue team runs — pipeline, deal cycles, quota, account planning, renewals — well enough to earn credibility with a quota-carrying rep, and who sees making Harvey's GTM team more effective with AI as the actual job.

What You'll Do

  • Bring order to and extend GTM's AI footprint. Audit the skills, plugins, and agents GTM teams have built; measure what's actually used; consolidate duplicates into well-maintained versions; retire what isn't earning its place; ship new AI-powered workflows.

  • Be the AI tooling partner of choice for GTM teams. Embed with Sales, CS, SDR, Legal Engineering, and Partnerships to understand their workflows from the inside — prospecting, call prep, follow-up, account planning, pricing, renewals — and steer them toward solutions that fit how they work rather than building for its own sake.

  • Own the intake for new AI features and experiments. GTM regularly asks to try new capabilities as they ship. Partner with fellow AI Enablement Engineers to build a lightweight path for requesting, piloting, and evaluating them — success criteria up front, a timebox, and a clear adopt / wait / pass call at the end — so experimentation stays fast without leaving another trail of abandoned tools.

  • Own technical governance of GTM skills and plugins. Define publishing standards, ownership, review, and deprecation rules for the GTM side of the plugin and skill marketplace, and stand up usage and spend monitoring so adoption, cost, and staleness stay visible as adoption scales.

  • Own the MCP and connector roadmap for GTM systems. Harden and extend the integrations GTM workflows depend on — Salesforce, Gong meeting notes and call recording, Gmail and Calendar, Slack, Omni, and internal knowledge sources — with sensible read/write scoping and guardrails around anything that reaches customers or prospects.

  • Build reference patterns GTM can extend. Ship well-structured templates and examples so GTM builders can create good workflows themselves, within guardrails, without you becoming the bottleneck for every new idea.

  • Run AI vendor reviews for GTM tools. AI sales tools pitch GTM leaders constantly. Partner with Privacy, Security, and Legal to evaluate them against a reusable framework and give a clear build / buy / pilot / pass recommendation.

What You Have

  • 5+ years of software, integration, or GTM engineering experience, with at least 2 years building integrations or automation on top of GTM systems (CRM, sales engagement, conversation intelligence, CPQ, analytics).

  • A real understanding of how GTM teams work — the sales cycle, pipeline management, account planning, renewals and expansion — ideally from having worked inside or alongside a revenue org. You can talk to a rep about their week, not just their data.

  • Hands-on experience with API integration patterns, OAuth and identity, webhook architectures, and the kind of glue work that makes enterprise systems actually talk to each other reliably.

  • Practical experience with LLM-based applications and AI tooling — prompt design, agent workflows, retrieval, evaluation, or production integration of model APIs. You don't need to have trained a model; you do need to have shipped something real that depends on one.

  • Working knowledge of the Model Context Protocol (MCP) or comparable agent-tool integration patterns. If you haven't shipped MCP yet, you've at minimum read the spec and built something against it.

  • A product mindset about internal tools. You measure adoption, talk to your users, and are as comfortable deprecating something as shipping it.

  • Strong communication and stakeholder-management instincts with GTM leaders and individual contributors — you can redirect a VP's feature request toward a better solution and keep the relationship, and be the most pragmatic person in an engineering review the same afternoon.

  • Strong DevOps and operational fundamentals — CI/CD, infrastructure-as-code, secrets management, and observability. You treat the integrations and AI tools you ship as production systems: version-controlled, monitored, and safe to change without breaking the teams that depend on them.

  • Demonstrated experience applying data governance and security best practices, including to customer data and to agents that take external-facing actions.

  • Comfort evaluating third-party vendors — asking the right questions about data access and flows, reading DPAs, and translating findings into clear go/no-go recommendations for the business.

  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, high-growth, and global environment with significant ambiguity.

Bonus Points:

  • Background as a GTM Engineer, RevOps or Sales Ops engineer, Solutions Engineer, or Forward Deployed Engineer — ideally combined with internal tooling work.

  • Experience at a company where sales and CS teams adopted AI tooling at scale, and first-hand lessons about what stuck and what didn't.

  • Hands-on work with Salesforce (including custom development), sales engagement platforms, CPQ, or conversation intelligence tools, including their APIs or AI-adjacent extensions.

  • Familiarity with enterprise iPaaS platforms.

  • Experience leading change management or enablement for a sales organization.

Compensation

$153,000 - $210,500 USD
